status.description: done = every done-criterion met AND every hard stop declared as not fired. blocked = a decision is needed that the lane does not authorize, or a hard stop fired; stop, do not guess. deviated = the work was completed but required departing from the stated approach or touching a path outside allowed_paths. failed = could not complete for a technical reason. interaction_required = the worker needs a human/orchestrator answer to proceed and has stopped.

summary.description: What was actually done, in two or three sentences. No preamble.

hard_stops.description: MANDATORY. One entry for every hard stop listed in the lane, whether or not it fired. A result that omits a hard stop is invalid regardless of its criteria — this field exists because green criteria have twice hidden a violated hard stop.

hard_stop.description: The hard stop as written in the lane.

fired.description: true means the condition was reached. If any is true, status must be blocked.

note.description: Required when fired is true: what was encountered, and what was NOT done as a result.

files_changed.description: Every canonical path change INSIDE the worktree. Copies require both source_path and destination path.

external_changes.description: Every path created, modified, or deleted OUTSIDE the worktree — configuration files, dotfiles, machine-level setup. Git never saw this work, so there is no diff, no branch, and no undo except what this entry records.

path.description: Absolute, or ~-prefixed. NOT worktree-relative — never a path files_changed could also hold.

why.description: Required: a change outside the repository always needs its reason stated; unlike files_changed, there is no diff to infer it from.

revert.description: Required: the backup path or exact command that restores the previous state. Mandatory because git cannot undo this — the envelope is the only record of how.

done_criteria.description: One entry per done-criterion from the lane, with evidence.

evidence.description: Command output, file:line, or test result. Not an assertion that it works. For a criterion about something being consumed, the evidence must name the terminal consumer — the program or file that reads the value — not another mention of its name.

commit.description: The commit that carries this work. Omitted on a read-only lane; the binary does not trust this field for enforcement.

questions.description: Required when status is blocked. Each question must be answerable without reading the worktree.

why_blocking.description: What cannot proceed until this is answered.

options.description: Candidate answers, if the fork is closed-ended.

deviations.description: Required when status is deviated. Anything done differently from the lane, or any path touched outside allowed_paths.

findings.description: Things discovered that the lane did not ask about but that change other work. This is how a sweep pays for itself.

skills_loaded.description: Obsolete and ignored by lucind-ai. Kept so older envelopes validate. Agents report it unreliably, so do not use it as evidence.

session_id.description: Conversation or session id needed to resume this lane.
